Article Title: Jack Dorsey has been renovating his sprawling $32 million mansion for over 14 years; his utlra-rich neighbours can't stop complaining
Article Text:
In pic: Jack Dorsey

Two properties, one long project

Sauna complex, plunge pool and rooftop gardens

Estate expands beyond a single property

A neighbourhood-wide building boom

Even in one of San Francisco's wealthiest neighbourhoods, money cannot always buy peace and quiet. Jack Dorsey, the Twitter co-founder and chief executive of fintech company Block, has spent nearly 14 years renovating and expanding his oceanfront properties in the exclusive Sea Cliff neighbourhood, a project that neighbours say has turned the area into a long-running construction zone, according to a report by the New York Post. Residents told the publication that the sounds of jackhammers, cement mixers and construction vehicles have become a fixture of daily life as work on Dorsey's luxury compound continues years after it began. “I've been listening to 24-7 construction noise in the distance for years now,” one resident told the Post anonymously. “One day it will end. I hope.”Dorsey, 49, who now leads financial technology company Block, owns two adjoining properties in the exclusive Sea Cliff enclave. They overlook the Pacific Ocean and the Golden Gate Bridge and cover a combined 1.21 acres on El Camino del Mar. According to SFGate, jackhammers, cement mixers and construction trucks have been heard in the area for over a decade. He bought the first property in February 2012 for $9.99 million. The 3,734-square-foot modernist home, built in 1965, originally had two bedrooms and two bathrooms. Construction began within months and has continued in various forms since.City records show a major redevelopment application filed in December 2013 proposed $3.7 million in improvements, including seismic upgrades, extra living space, roof decks and a planted roof. That permit alone took three and a half years to obtain. A 2020 redesign changed the windows, courtyard and exterior finishes, and was approved in July 2022. Later applications covered solar panels, landscaping, fire sprinklers, retaining walls, an underground water tank and a cold plunge pool.As per the report, the architectural plans seen by the local media suggests that the Dorsey is creating a highly customised retreat. The redesigned property consists of vegetation-covered roofs, reclaimed redwood cladding, extensive stonework and large ocean-facing windows. The standout feature of the luxurious property is a private hot tub connected to the primary bedroom, a steam room, plunge pool, gym, outdoor fire pit and an expansive sauna complex with its own dedicated access areas. The renovation plan also include dozens of solar panels and a sophisticated fire-protection system which need more than 100 sprinklers and a dedicated water line.The project grew even larger in 2018 when Dorsey acquired the neighbouring property for $21.9 million, bringing his total acquisition costs to approximately $31.9 million.The second home spans about 3,588 square feet and sits on more than half an acre. While restrictions separating the two properties have reportedly been removed, available plans do not indicate that the homes will be physically merged into a single structure.The expansion mirrors a broader trend among technology billionaires assembling large residential compounds. The New York Post noted that Mark Zuckerberg has purchased multiple neighbouring properties around Lake Tahoe, while Sam Altman has also expanded his real-estate footprint around his San Francisco residence.While Dorsey's project has attracted attention because of its longevity, it is not the only source of disruption in Sea Cliff. The affluent neighbourhood, which has been home to figures including late comedian Robin Williams, actress Sharon Stone, Salesforce co-founder Marc Benioff and investor Tom Steyer, is experiencing a broader construction surge.Planning records cited in the report indicate that at least 24 homes along the eight-block stretch of El Camino del Mar have filed building permits since the start of 2025. Recent observations by local media found scaffolding, construction crews and heavy equipment operating outside several multimillion-dollar residences. For some residents, the combination of luxury home renovations and constant tourism has become an unexpected downside of living in one of San Francisco's most exclusive enclaves.Despite the complaints, there is no indication that Dorsey's renovation project is nearing completion, leaving some neighbours hoping that the sounds of construction will eventually give way to the tranquillity usually associated with a multimillion-dollar oceanfront address.
Article Summary: Twitter co-founder and chief executive of fintech company Block, Jack Dorsey, owns two properties in San Francisco's exclusive Sea Cliff neighbourhood. Dorsey bought the first property in February 2012 for $9.99 million. Construction began within months and has continued in various forms since. Neighbours say the sounds of jackhammers, cement mixers and construction vehicles have become a fixture of daily life.

Article Title: Michael Dell is funding South Korea's most-expensive divorce ever; putting $406 million from family fund into SK Group
Article Text:
Michael and wife Susan Dell

How Michael Dell is helping SK chairman’s $711 million divorce

Dell’s link to SK Group

Michael Dell is putting $406 million into South Korea’s SK Group, buying shares from chairman Chey Tae-wo. According to a Reuters report, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million). The deal is part of Chey Tae-Won’s plan to raise 944 billion won through share sales to pay a divorce settlement to his former wife.Earlier this month, SK Inc said in ​a filing that Chey Tae-Won had agreed to sell 1.65 million shares, or a 2.26% stake for ​944 billion won. Of those, DFO Public Investments, L.P., a Delaware-based investment fund ​affiliated with DFO Management, the family investment office of Michael Dell, agreed to buy 972,493 SK ​Inc shares.The sale covers the bigger part of a 944 billion won ($711 million) share sale to fund the payout to Roh Soh-yeong, director of Seoul's Art Center Nabi and the daughter of former South Korean president Roh Tae-woo.The rest of the money will come from a price return swap with Korea Investment & Securities, a Seoul brokerage, covering 681,431 shares, or 0.94% of SK Inc., for about 400 billion won ($301 million). Both transactions are due to settle on November 2.Dell Technologies, a major supplier of AI servers and data ‌centre ⁠infrastructure, has business ties with SK Hynix, SK Group's memory chipmaking unit. It supplies chips for Dell's data center servers.Michael Dell, 61, has a net worth of about $241.3 billion, making him the world's fifth-richest person. His wealth has grown as Dell Technologies' shares have risen and through his large stake in chipmaker Broadcom. He received the Broadcom shares when he sold software company VMware to Broadcom in 2023.
Article Summary: Michael Dell is putting $406 million into South Korea’s SK Group, buying shares from chairman Chey Tae-wo. Dell Technologies, a major supplier of AI servers and data ‌centre ⁠infrastructure, has business ties with SK Hynix, SK Group's memory chipmaking unit.

Article Title: Melinda French Gates gives 'guided office tour' to show 'few things that bring me JOY'; expands on the sentiment that women ...
Article Text:
Ginsburg quote remains a source of inspiration

A reminder of progress for women

The artwork behind her desk

Focus on women’s health

Bill Gates ex-wife and philanthropist Melinda Gates has offered followers a glimpse inside her office, showcasing three personal items that she says bring her joy while also reinforcing her long-standing advocacy for women’s advancement and leadership. In a video shared on social media platform Instagram, the Gates showed the viewers what she described as tour of “a few things that bring me JOY in my office.” The video shared featured various items such as a figurine of late US Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, a vintage board game titled “The Exciting Game of Career Girls,” and a piece of artwork displaying the word “JOY.” As per an Inc. report, the video has been viewed by more than 1.2 million people.Among the items, French Gates highlighted a figurine gifted by her younger brother that honours Ginsburg, whom she described as a major influence. She used the item to draw attention to one of the late justice's most widely cited observations: “Women belong in all places where decisions are made.” According to the report, French Gates also displayed a framed version of the quote signed by Ginsburg.The message aligns closely with French Gates' philanthropic work, which has focused heavily on improving opportunities for women and families.Through Pivotal, the organisation she founded in 2015, she has directed significant investments toward women's health and gender equality initiatives. Earlier this year, she pledged an additional $215 million to the organisation, bringing her total commitment over the previous two years to $600 million to support areas including contraception and maternal healthcare, according to Pivotal.Another item featured in the office tour was “The Exciting Game of Career Girls,” a board game from the 1950s. The game, which depicts careers such as nurse, stewardess and teacher as desirable options for women, serves as a reminder of how opportunities have expanded over time, French Gates said. “It reminds me that we actually have made a lot of progress when you think about all the different types of careers women have these days,” she said, according to the report. The comments expand on a theme that has long shaped her public advocacy: increasing women's participation in leadership roles and decision-making positions across society.The final item in the office tour was a large artwork reading “JOY,” which hangs above her desk. According to French Gates, the letters are composed of numerous small human figures, symbolising the idea of shared happiness and community. “Each little blob represents a different person, and it's a representation of collective joy,” she said. “If we have joy in our lives, if we share it with somebody else, it doubles that joy. ” She added that the artwork frequently draws comments from people during video calls, with many noticing the word displayed behind her and responding positively to it.French Gates’s philanthropy centres on advancing women and families. In 2015 she founded Pivotal, an organisation focused on women’s health. Earlier this year she pledged an additional $215 million to it, bringing her total commitment over the past two years to $600 million, according to Pivotal’s website. The money is meant to expand global access to contraceptives and maternal care.
Article Summary: Melinda Gates shared a video of three personal items that she says bring her joy. The items include a figurine of late US Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, a vintage board game titled “The Exciting Game of Career Girls,” and a piece of artwork displaying the word “JOY.”

Article Title: As California’s billionaire tax faces defeat, problems for wealthy tech execs may not be over
Article Text:
Countermeasures seal Prop 40’s fate

Mixed results for wealth taxes across other US states

Federal scrutiny awaits in Democrat controlled Congress

California’s ultra-wealthy tech executives appear on the verge of defeating a state wealth tax, but their tax battles are far from finished. While election officials continue counting ballots, early returns show 56% of California voters rejecting Proposition 40, compared to 44% in favour. As the ballot measure requires a simple majority to pass, election analysts say defeat is virtually assured, as per a report by CNBC. The measure sought to impose a one-time 5% levy on the net worth of California residents holding more than $1 billion in assets.While Silicon Valley billionaires breathe a sigh of relief at home, tax experts warn that the state-level fight could catalyse a much broader push in Washington, where newly empowered Democrats in Congress are eyeing federal tax increases on top earners and a potential federal wealth tax, the report added.The billionaire tax ran into direct opposition from two competing ballot measures designed as legislative countermeasures.Proposition 41: Restricts how state tax revenue can be spent.Proposition 42: Explicitly prohibits the state from taxing personal assets.Both countermeasures are currently winning majority support among voters. Under California election rules, if either proposition receives more total votes than Proposition 40, the billionaire tax is officially nullified, the report added.Faced with the mounting deficit, the proposal’s primary backer conceded defeat with the healthcare union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW West) announcing plans to reintroduce the initiative in 2028 unless state lawmakers intervene to “make billionaires pay their fair share.”While California voters rejected taxing accumulated net worth, measures aimed at taxing high-income earners saw stronger momentum elsewhere. In Washington State, voters approved a new “millionaire tax,” establishing a 9.9% tax rate on household income exceeding $1 million per year.In Colorado, a ballot measure seeking to replace the state’s 4.4% flat tax with a graduated income tax, featuring an 8.4% top bracket on earnings above $1 million, remains too close to call.With Democrats now positioned to take control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, tax policy analysts anticipate a wave of federal legislation designed to increase levies on wealthy individuals and corporations to fund middle-class relief.“It is clear Democrats will try to lower taxes for middle-income households and raise taxes on certain businesses and high-income households. But it is much too soon to know how,” said Howard Gleckman, nonresident fellow at the Tax Policy Center, as per CNBC.Federal lawmakers could revive legislative frameworks introduced during the last congressional cycle by Democratic Senators Chris Van Hollen of Maryland and Cory Booker of New Jersey. Van Hollen’s proposal introduces a graduated surtax on incomes surpassing $1 million:$1 Million to $2 Million: A 5% surtax.Over $5 Million: A 12% surtax.Top Marginal Income Rate: Would rise to 49%, up from the current 37% federal ceiling.Capital Gains: The top long-term capital gains tax rate would jump from 23.8% to 35.8%.To counterbalance the tax hikes, the plan proposes expanding exemptions for middle- and lower-income filers, creating a $46,000 deduction for single tax filers and a $92,000 deduction for joint filers.
Article Summary: California voters reject a state wealth tax on ultra-wealthy tech executives. Prop 40 requires a simple majority to pass, but election analysts say defeat is virtually assured. Newly empowered Democrats in Congress are eyeing federal tax increases on top earners and a potential federal wealth tax.

Article Title: World’s most valuable company CEO loses spot in world’s top 10 richest, loses $15 billion in a day
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

$2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq in one day

Why tech companies lost billions recently

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang lost his place in the world’s top 15 richest billionaires. According to Bloomberg, the tech billionaire lost nearly $15.1 billion in a day after the company’s stocks tumbled following Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm election. The loss dropped him to 13th from ninth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Other billionaires whose wealth declined were Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Oracle founder Larry Ellison, who lost $79.7 billion and $10.1 billion, respectively.The decline comes after the Nasdaq 100 index erased $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day on November 5 as Nvidia and other major technology companies suffered steep losses amid growing fears over the future of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending in the US. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5% on Thursday, marking its biggest one-day drop since the market sell-off triggered by US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025.The fall hit major tech companies include Nvidia and AMD whose shares dropped by 9% and 17% during Thursday’s trading session. Notably, Nvidia hit a market capitalization of $5.02 trillion earlier this week, regaining the title of world’s most valuable company from Apple.The Democrats’ strong performance in the US midterm elections has raised concerns that local opposition and tighter scrutiny could slow the construction of new data centres. Several incoming Democratic governors, including in Texas, have called for an immediate moratorium on data centre development.Data centres require large amounts of electricity and water, raising concerns among communities about pressure on power grids and local resources. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses.Analysts have warned that the AI boom may be entering a phase where companies are judged not just on their growth potential but also on the cost of building and operating their infrastructure.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang lost nearly $15.1 billion in a day after the company’s stocks tumbled following Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm election. The loss dropped him to 13th from ninth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Other billionaires whose wealth declined were Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Oracle founder Larry Ellison.

Article Title: Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards
Article Text:
Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards

Gigabyte has launched its Gigabyte 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign to mark its 40th anniversary, offering consumers a chance to win Amazon gift vouchers, monitors, AORUS merchandise and other products. The campaign will run from November 1 to December 31, 2026, and is open to residents of India. The campaign will feature three activities: Build a Rig, Play a Run and Share Your Story. Consumers can participate by purchasing eligible Gigabyte products, playing a browser-based game or sharing stories about their Gigabyte hardware.Under the Build a Rig activity, Gigabyte is offering rewards through its AORUS Full House programme. Consumers purchasing eligible Gigabyte and AORUS products can earn Amazon gift vouchers based on the number of product categories included in their PC build.The vouchers are worth up to Rs 15,500. Participants with complete builds can also receive AORUS merchandise, while select AORUS INFINITY products qualify for an additional bonus.The Play a Run activity features AORUS Infinity Run, a free browser-based game that takes players through five eras of hardware, from 1986 to the AI era.Each run lasts up to 90 seconds, and players do not need to log in. Participants can submit one entry per day after completing a run. Every valid entry will be included in a monthly random draw for a Gigabyte monitor.Players can also share their scorecards on Instagram by tagging @aorus_in and using the hashtag #MyGigabyte to participate in AORUS merchandise giveaways.The Share Your Story activity, called Still Running, invites consumers to share their experiences with Gigabyte products they have owned. Participants can write about hardware that remains in their PC, has been passed on to someone else or has been retired. Stories can be submitted on Instagram using @aorus_in and hashtags #MyGigabyte or #ENTERINFINITYINDIA, through the pinned Still Running thread on the r/aorusin Reddit community, or via an online form.More than 20 prizes are available, including at least three Gigabyte products. A Gigabyte India panel will select monthly winners across four categories: Best Story, Best Second Life, Most Loyal Builder and Still Running.The campaign activities opened on November 1, 2026, at 12am IST and will close on December 31, 2026, at 11:59pm IST. November winners will be announced in the first week of December 2026, while December winners will be announced in the first week of January 2027.Gigabyte said the campaign will run through its India community channels on Instagram and Reddit. Two of the three activities are free to enter, and participants can submit their stories in any language.Commenting on the campaign, Sunil Grewal, Director, Gigabyte India, said, “Forty years is a long time in an industry where hardware changes every year or two. What has carried us through is the trust of people who build their own PCs and expect them to keep running long after the build is done. ENTER INFINITY is our way of handing this anniversary to them. Whether someone is building a new rig this festive season, playing a quick run, or telling us about a Gigabyte motherboard that is still running years later, we want our next chapter in India to be shaped by those experiences.
Article Summary: Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards. The campaign will run from November 1 to December 31, 2026, and is open to residents of India. Consumers can participate by purchasing eligible Gigabyte products, playing a browser-based game or sharing stories about their Gigabyte hardware.

Article Title: In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters and $423,000 to buy laptops for students; he also pledged that he would 'fund fixing the water in any house that has ...'
Article Text:
Elon Musk's donations during the Flint crisis

Clean drinking water returns to schools

Delays before rollout

Flint's recovery efforts continue

In 2018, the SpaceX CEO Elon Musk’s foundation donated about $480,000 to install water filtration systems in Flint, Michigan, schools, along with $423,000 for student laptops. The foundation funded 136 filtering stations that serve twelve school buildings. The donation came years after Flint’s water supply was contaminated with catastrophic levels of lead in 2014, when officials switched to a cheaper water source.Podcaster and former advisor to the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), Katie Miller also recently shared a post on X highlighting the impact of the project. In the post, she noted that the Musk Foundation donated ultraviolet water filtration systems and new drinking stations across all 12 Flint Community Schools buildings as well as the district's administration building. She also pointed out that the city separately provided free water filters for residential homes.The donation made by Elon Musk’s Foundation dates back to 2018, when the organisation contributed around $480,350 to fund water filtration systems for Flint schools and an additional $423,000 to purchase laptops for students. Around the same time, Musk also pledged that he would "fund fixing the water in any house in Flint that has water contamination above FDA levels," as the city continued to deal with the fallout from its water crisis.The water crisis at Flint started in 2014, when the officials switched to a cheaper water source, which led to widespread lead contamination of water that affected thousands of residents. The water crisis also led to national outrage and prompted support from charities, public agencies and private donors asking for help for the affected communities.According to a report by The Independent, students in Flint were eventually able to drink directly from school water fountains for the first time in years after the Musk-funded filtration systems became operational. The foundation donated 136 filtering stations that serve school buildings throughout the district. Speaking at a ceremony marking the rollout of the new fountains, Kevelin Jones, superintendent of Flint Community Schools, said access to clean water should be a basic necessity rather than something families have to struggle to obtain. Before the filtration systems were activated, the district had relied on bottled water for several years.The filtration systems use advanced technology designed to remove contaminants, including lead, from drinking water. Before being placed into service, they were tested by researchers from Kettering University and independent environmental experts to ensure they met safety standards.The project also faced a lot of challenges. The installation of the filtration stations faced a lot of delays and also needed reconfiguration before they could be implemented completely. Once fully functional, the students welcomed the change after years without access to drinking fountains. One of the students also told the local media that it felt "amazing" to finally have clean water available at school. This change marked a significant moment for the district as it had depended on bottled water since the beginning of the crisis.The residents however appreciated the support, but some community leaders also agreed that water filters alone cannot solve the bigger problems caused on the infrastructure due to this water crisis. Former Flint Mayor Karen Weaver said in 2018 that in order to completely restore the trust of the public we need to replace the damaged water infrastructure and also lead service lines throughout the city.Since then, Flint has continued its recovery efforts. City officials have reported significant progress in inspecting service lines and replacing thousands of lead and galvanized steel pipes as part of the long-term effort to restore confidence in the city's water system.
Article Summary: Elon Musk’s foundation donated $480,350 to Flint schools in 2018. The money was used to install water filtration systems and buy laptops for students. The donation came years after Flint's water supply was contaminated with catastrophic levels of lead in 2014.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman reacts to Delaware’s AI agent proposal, says it is ‘deeply concerning to …’
Article Text:
What is Delaware Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC)

Congress threatens intervention

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned against a legislative proposal in Delaware that would permit autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to legally manage and operate corporate entities. Suleyman pushed back the state’s initiative, saying that granting legal corporate status to autonomous software demands extreme scrutiny, and calling it ‘deeply concerning’. Not just tech leaders, the proposal also sparked sharp backlash from federal lawmakers like Representative James Comer (R-Ky.), chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.“Deeply concerning to me... Delaware proposal to let agents run businesses... we should be very cautious here,” Suleyman stated on social media platform X (formerly Twitter). Quoting directly from the framework's core premise, Suleyman highlighted the far-reaching nature of the concept:“A Delaware AIC will be a separate legal entity whose day-to-day affairs are managed by an AI agent rather than a person. At the agent’s direction, the AIC can sue and be sued in its own name, hold and dispose of property, and incur obligations...”Delaware, widely recognised as America’s premier hub for corporate incorporations, is exploring a new business structure titled an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC). According to a draft bill that may go before the Delaware State Legislature, the framework aims to introduce a 30-month “regulatory sandbox” to pilot the concept, bringing in additional state revenue through corporate filing fees and taxes.Under the provisions of the draft bill, an AIC could operate with any lawful commercial purpose, whether for-profit or non-profit, with the sole explicit restriction being the business of banking. Moreover, an AI agent could be formally designated to oversee day-to-day affairs, enter into contracts, make commercial transactions, and direct business strategy without a human at the helm.At the direction of its designated AI agent, the company could hold or dispose of real and personal property, incur financial obligations, and initiate or face legal lawsuits in its own corporate name.The prospect of shielding corporate backers from AI misbehaviour has triggered an immediate counter-offensive in Washington. Last month, Representative Comer sent a formal inquiry to Delaware Governor Matt Meyer demanding documents regarding the AIC framework and its associated safety risks.Comer warned that the mechanism creates a dangerous loophole:“We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives.”Comer warned that federal legislation could be introduced to directly preempt state-level AI efforts.
Article Summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned against a legislative proposal in Delaware that would permit autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to legally manage and operate corporate entities. The proposal has sparked sharp backlash from federal lawmakers like Representative James Comer (R-Ky), chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

Article Title: After reported cases of broken bones, brain damage and other injuries; US Consumer Product Safety Commission issues red alert; tells Lowe’s, Costco and Amazon to recall 3.6 million …
Article Text:
Pic courtesy: US Consumer Product Safety Commission website

What US CPSC 'red notice' says

Which ladder models are being recalled

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has issued an alert notifying consumers across America that 3.6 million ladders are being recalled because they could unexpectedly retract due to faulty locks. According to reports, warning comes after a number of people sustained broken bones, brain damage and other injuries.US CPSC has published a recall notice warning consumers that approximately 3,662,000 (3.6 million) ladders made by Little Giant Ladder Systems were being recalled after the company received several reports of the ladders unexpectedly retracting, causing serious injuries to users. As per CPSC's warning to buyers: "Ladders can suddenly retract if the Rapid Locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard to consumers. "The faulty ladders have been sold on Lowes, Amazon, Costco, LittleGiantLadders and other websites. As per the consumer body, the 3.6 million-plus ladders included in this recall were sold nationally between December 2015 and October 2026. The ladders sold are priced anywhere from around $100 to around $1,000.The CPSC's notice says that the Rapid Locks are black or orange components on the ladders’ legs, designed to be inserted to adjust the ladders’ height.When the Rapid Locks don’t work as intended, the ladders can suddenly retract, causing the user to fall and sustain serious injuries. Little Giant has also published its own recall notice, in which the ladder manufacturer warns of the same hazard."Consumers should stop using the recalled ladders immediately until they review the information at http://www.littlegiantladders.com/pages/recalls or via the QR code on the ladder and contact Little Giant for a repair kit containing warning labels and instructions. The additional instructions and labels, which should be affixed to the ladder, advise consumers to verify that their Rapid Locks are properly engaged before every use and to maintain their locks with lubrication. Consumers who follow the provided instructions and have a Rapid Lock that does not function properly after the application of lubrication should contact Little Giant for evaluation. If a lock does not function properly after this evaluation, the company will offer the choice of a replacement ladder of the same or equivalent model or a refund ranging from a depreciated value determined by date of purchase up to full purchase price for ladders purchased within the past 12 months," said the USCPC on its page.The CPSC says the following models of Little Giant ladders are being recalled: Adjustable Fortress 2.0, Conquest 2.0, Dark Horse 2.0, Epic, King Kombo XT, Leveler, MegaLite, MegaLite+, Multi, Quantum and Vector.

Article Title: Oracle troubles aggravate as Microsoft scraps 3-year-old deal; comes as software giant rethinks cloud partnerships; renting computing from Oracle reportedly became less useful as ...
Article Text:
Microsoft 'refuses' to expand Texas data center deal with Nscale

Microsoft is phasing out an artificial intelligence (AI) computing partnership with Oracle Corp after choosing not to renew a 2023 agreement, Bloomberg has reported, citing people familiar with the matter. According to the report, Microsoft has steadily deactivated rented server capacity in recent months. The Oracle-hosted machines relied on older generations of Nvidia Corp. chips that no longer align with Microsoft's current computing requirements. The shift highlights growing industry unease surrounding hardware obsolescence; research firm Gartner Inc. has warned that aggressive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure risk significant write-downs as faster, more efficient chips enter the market.The loss of capacity utilization compounds existing headwinds for Oracle. Substantial capital outlays toward AI data center construction have driven the company’s free cash flow into negative territory, leaving its credit rating hovering just one level above junk status. Oracle’s stock has fallen by more than half since reaching a high in June.Neither company disclosed the total financial value of the contract when it was announced in 2023 to support Microsoft’s AI-powered Bing search engine, and Bloomberg was unable to determine its full scale.The wind-down follows an earlier report by Business Insider indicating that separate negotiations to lease additional Oracle capacity broke down in June this year.Oracle shares dropped roughly 3% following the news. An Oracle spokesperson stated that customer demand for its AI infrastructure remains robust, including for earlier-generation hardware. The non-renewal comes as Microsoft actively reviews more than $80 billion in outside cloud computing commitments across providers including CoreWeave, Nscale, and Nebius Group. Company executives have grown increasingly dissatisfied with escalating expenses and operational delays across these third-party agreements, Bloomberg reported. The tech giant recently passed on an option to expand an Nscale deployment in Texas, coming just weeks after it withdrew from a planned Nscale site in the UK.Microsoft will reportedly not exercise an option to more than double the size ​of its existing agreement with AI cloud provider Nscale to rent more ‌computing power at a Texas data center. According to a report in The Financial Times, a potential deal extension would have been ​worth tens of billions of dollars for Nscale. The companies struck ​a deal in 2025 for Nscale to deploy around 200,000 Nvidia AI chips under ​an expanded agreement with Microsoft across its data centers in Europe and the US.The development comes weeks ‌after ⁠Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's flagship data center project in Loughton, Essex, after power connection delays pushed its expected supply date into the 2030s.

According to the report, Microsoft has steadily deactivated rented server capacity in recent months. The Oracle-hosted machines relied on older generations of Nvidia Corp. chips that no longer align with Microsoft's current computing requirements.

OKXICE’s plan for blockchain-based stock trading meets rising corporate resistance. The joint venture led by crypto firm OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, proposed round-the-clock trading in tokenised shares of 62 public companies. However, 54 companies in that original lineup had objected to their inclusion, according to the Fortune report. The opposition includes Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, JPMorgan Chase and Walmart, putting much of the proposed offering at risk.Co-chaired by former New York governor Andrew Cuomo, the venture has not confirmed whether the objections will change its launch plans. The resistance nevertheless exposes a central challenge: regulatory permission to offer tokenised stocks does not guarantee that the companies behind those stocks will accept the arrangement.Tokenised shares are digital representations of stocks recorded on a blockchain, a shared digital ledger. OKXICE proposed using that technology to offer trading beyond conventional stock-market hours.The venture comes after a temporary exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission in September. It allows qualifying platforms to trade tokenised stocks without registering as national securities exchanges, under certain conditions.Those conditions include notifying a company before offering shares tokenised by an unaffiliated third party and giving it an opportunity to object. The SEC also requires qualifying tokens to provide the same rights and privileges as equivalent traditional shares.According to Fortune, companies have 30 days from the date they receive notice to object and block their inclusion on the platform.Fortune reported that Boeing and ServiceNow joined the objection list this week, following Apple, Home Depot, and GE Vernova the day before.The resistance also extended beyond the venture’s original selection. Wells Fargo, Nebius Group, Arm Holdings, Cerebras Systems and Cigna Group were among companies outside that lineup that filed objections.Applied Optoelectronics, a networking equipment manufacturer that objected, previously told Fortune that the framework’s potential effects on its stock remained unclear.Its concerns included pricing, liquidity, which means how easily shares can be bought or sold and volatility, meaning fluctuations in price. However, the absence of an objection does not mean a company endorses the venture.

Article Title: Nvidia is providing billions of dollars to expand advanced AI chip-packaging capacity at a Taiwanese supplier as a manufacturing bottleneck threatens to slow production of powerful processors
Article Text:
AI chip

Supply cracks at TSMC force chipmakers to look elsewhere

Why packaging now commands half the value

The rise of panel-level packaging

Nvidia is reportedly pouring billions of dollars into expanding advanced chip-packaging capacity at a Taiwanese supplier as severe manufacturing bottlenecks threaten to slow the delivery of high-performance artificial intelligence (AI) processors. The move comes as the global race to build AI infrastructure has unleashed unprecedented capital into advanced packaging – a stage of semiconductor manufacturing once viewed as routine, but now standing as the primary choke point in producing next-generation hardware.Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) currently dominates the market for the most sophisticated packaging technologies, primarily Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS). This method mounts individual silicon dies, such as processors and high-bandwidth memory, onto a shared base so they can transfer data at high speeds.CoWoS is essential for processors designed by Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, as well as custom silicon created by major cloud providers. However, TSMC’s limited packaging capacity has left chip designers scrambling to find alternatives.To bypass the squeeze, Nvidia is providing billions of dollars in financing to expand CoWoS capacity at Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL), a subsidiary of Taiwan’s ASE Technology, news agency Reuters cited an industry executive familiar with the situation, as saying.Notably, Nvidia is not alone in funding external capacity. Rival AMD has announced plans to invest more than $10 billion across Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem, striking partnerships with ASE, SPIL and Powertech Technology.“I think CoWoS and advanced packaging are super important for our high-performance computing going forward. TSMC has been an incredible partner in advanced packaging, and we're going to continue to do more together. And yes, we do need more capacity overall,” AMD CEO Lisa Su told Reuters during an October visit to Taipei.For decades, packaging was an afterthought aimed at encasing chips in plastic or ceramic to protect them and connect them to circuit boards. “Packaging was always that thing that you just didn't worry about,” former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger, now a partner at Playground Global, said recently in Taipei. That dynamic has flipped as shrinking transistors onto single silicon slabs becomes increasingly difficult and expensive. Today's GPUs and CPUs frequently combine anywhere from 10 to 20 distinct chips into a single package. Gelsinger estimates advanced packaging could eventually account for as much as half of a chip’s total value.AI chips rely heavily on this integration because training and running large models requires immense amounts of data to move between compute dies and memory banks without delay.TSMC’s tight lines have created major openings for secondary packaging firms like Taiwan’s Powertech Technology (PTI).“Everyone is looking for a solution outside TSMC. They don't want to rely entirely on TSMC,” Powertech Chairman D.K. Tsai said in August.PTI is betting on panel-level packaging, which processes chips on wide rectangular panels instead of conventional round silicon wafers. The format fits more units per run and cuts material waste – a key benefit as AI chips grow physically larger.PTI is collaborating with AMD and Broadcom to prove the viability of panel packaging for large-scale AI applications. Powertech also plans to invest $400 million in an advanced packaging joint venture with Broadcom in Singapore, targeting production by 2028.
Article Summary: N Nvidia is reportedly pouring billions of dollars into expanding advanced chip- packaging capacity at a Taiwanese supplier. The move comes as severe manufacturing bottlenecks threaten to slow the delivery of high-performance artificial intelligence (AI) processors. TSMC’s limited packaging capacity has left chip designers scrambling to find alternatives.

Article Title: Goldman Sachs bans thousands of employees from using Claude Code and GitHub; company says: After a period of experimentation, we put them in the hands of those...
Article Text:
No more vibe coding for Goldman traders

Goldman's CIO was cheering vibe coding by traders in July

Goldman's AI policy reflects a wider Wall Street rethink

Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its staff from advanced AI coding tools, and not everyone at the bank is pleased. Access to tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub is now limited to engineers, according to internal guidance updated in October and seen by Bloomberg. Traders, bankers and other non-technical employees, many of whom had been using these tools for months, have lost access.The bank says the call came after it looked at productivity and risk. A Goldman spokesperson, Nick Carcaterra, told Bloomberg that the firm offers certain AI tools to staff so it can figure out where they work best. Once that trial period ends, the tools go "in the hands of those who are best suited to leverage them," he said.There is one exception. The rule does not apply to strats, Goldman's term for employees who sit between trading, quantitative research and software engineering.Traders seem to feel the change most. According to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg, some had been using the tools to track client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and put together written and graphic content. On a trading desk, losing that kind of speed is felt quickly.The reversal stands out because Goldman had been openly encouraging this. In July, chief information officer Marco Argenti spoke about vibe coding by traders and bankers. He described non-technical staff building their own fixes with AI and passing them to one of the firm's 12,000 engineers to refine.This is also not Goldman's first AI restriction. Earlier this year, the bank limited the use of Anthropic's Claude for its Hong Kong staff, though that rule applied only to that location.None of this means Goldman is stepping back from AI. It has built an in-house AI assistant that combines models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google parent Alphabet. In May, John Waldron, seen as the likely successor to CEO David Solomon, compared the bank to an assembly line run by people and said much of that work could be automated.Goldman isn't the only bank rethinking how its staff use AI. Firms across Wall Street are spending millions of dollars on these tools while also dealing with cybersecurity worries, rising bills and uneven productivity gains. Working out who should use what has become a task of its own.JPMorgan Chase said in July it wanted employees to match models to tasks, so the priciest option isn't used for something as basic as summarising an analyst report. The idea is to keep costs in check without slowing people down.Goldman's move follows a similar line, applied to coding assistants. Instead of opening every tool to every employee, the bank is deciding which roles need them and limiting access to those roles.For now, that means engineers and strats. The traders who had built daily workflows around Claude Code and GitHub will have to find another way to get that work done.
Article Summary: Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its staff from advanced AI coding tools. Access to tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub is now limited to engineers. Traders, bankers and other non-technical employees have lost access. Goldman says the call came after it looked at productivity and risk.

Article Title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal answers why he left his $35 billion company for Temple: A weekend project while I was still Zomato CEO ended in…
Article Text:
Deepinder Goyal explains why he left Zomato for Temple

Deepinder Goyal built Temple around his dislike of AI devices

Goyal answers doctors’ criticism with $20 million of his own money

Deepinder Goyal says Temple was never meant to be his next big bet. In a vision note titled “Humanity’s Last Personal Device”, the Zomato founder writes that he began building a health wearable as a weekend project while he was still CEO of Eternal, the company formerly known as Zomato. That project led to an engineering breakthrough, and the breakthrough is what pulled him out of Eternal to build Temple full-time.The note answers a question Goyal raised himself on X earlier in the day. Many people, he wrote, wanted to know why he would leave a roughly $35 billion company he founded 18 years ago to chase a niche health wearable. He conceded that it doesn’t sound like a rational move.Goyal’s reasoning starts with a grievance. He argues that privacy is a basic human right, and that every voice AI device sold as the next computing interface breaks it the moment its microphone switches on, because a mic records everyone in the room. He writes that he hates it when people walk into meetings with him with their AI note-taker running.Temple is his workaround. Instead of a mic, it reads the vibrations of the wearer’s voice through motion sensors, so it hears the person wearing it and nobody else. Goyal wrote, with an expletive, that there wasn’t even a word for that, so Temple invented one: “roomdeaf”.He is just as particular about what Temple won’t do. Goyal calls it a companion and not an assistant, because it will not shop for you and will stick to tasks that don’t need a screen.Personal devices, in his view, should get out of the way. He also writes that he sees Temple serving humanity in the space age, and suggests a few Black Mirror episodes as a reference for where it could go.Not everyone is sold. A section of Indian doctors has questioned Temple’s health claims on X, and Goyal replied with a seven-point post addressed to them.His first argument was commercial. Temple offers 14-day, no-questions-asked returns, which he noted even Apple doesn’t offer in India, so a device that failed to deliver would be exposed within days. He said Temple has cost $30 million so far, $20 million of it his own, and that a few thousand units would recover only a fraction of that. A scam that pays nothing, he wrote, isn’t one anyone would run.Then he made it personal. Goyal said he has enough money to last generations and would not stake a reputation built over 20 years on a quick buck. Temple’s employees invested in a round a few months ago, he added, and the round being raised now is mostly made up of customers.On the science, he pointed to Whoop, which shipped its band in 2015 and published validation a few years later. Temple’s pre-prints are coming, Goyal said, and its most groundbreaking features are still under wraps. He signed off by telling the doctors to keep raging if he hadn’t convinced them.Goyal calls Temple “a project, not a product” and says health remains its north star. Temple 01 ships in early 2027 with both AI and health features, pre-orders are open, and he is already talking about what Temple 20 might look like.The move he admits doesn’t look rational now has his money and a 20-year reputation riding on it.
Article Summary: Deepinder Goyal built Temple around his dislike of AI devices. Goyal says he has enough money to last generations and would not stake a reputation built over 20 years on a quick buck. Temple 01 ships in early 2027 with both AI and health features, pre-orders are open.

Article Title: Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam 'attacked'; months after balloons full of acidic mixture were thrown; riot police called in
Article Text:
Protestors outside Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam

Why people are protesting against Microsoft data centre

A group of protestors stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data centre located on the outskirts of Amsterdam on Friday (November 6), escalating European demonstrations targeting large-scale technology infrastructure. The latest ‘attack’ takes place just months after activists targeted the same location with acid-filled balloons. Riot police have been deployed which made multiple arrests. The breach occurred near Sloterdijk in Amsterdam’s western port area, where work is underway on a major three-building complex intended for Microsoft.As per a Reuters witness, approximately 100 people breached the site’s boundaries. However, a spokesperson for activist campaign group Geef Tegengas told local broadcaster AT5 that around 500 demonstrators entered the grounds, with hundreds more remaining outside. As per local news portal AN5, several protesters entered the facility by cutting or breaking through perimeter fences, while others scaled an on-site construction crane.Dutch news agency ANP reported that police had initially blocked the demonstration march earlier in the morning. After the city’s mayor issued an order banning the gathering, marchers attempted to push through established police lines before heading toward the building grounds.Geef Tegengas, an advocacy group that campaigns against fossil fuels, is demanding an immediate and permanent halt to the development due to straining power grids. The group claims the completed data centre will consume an amount of electricity equivalent to every household in Amsterdam combined, warning that the power drawn by the facility will derail the construction of 30,000 planned local homes.The development consists of three separate towers, each reaching a height of 85 metres, all of which will be leased entirely by Microsoft. Initial plans were submitted back in 2016, preceding a municipal ban enacted by Amsterdam on new data centre builds inside the city.Microsoft data centre is repeatedly being targeted in coordinated European actionThe November 6th’s security breach follows previous hostile actions directed at the exact same location. In July, members of Extinction Rebellion targeted the perimeter, throwing balloons loaded with paint and an acidic mixture over the security fences.Interestingly, Friday's demonstration was organised as part of a coordinated, two-day wave of protest actions scheduled across multiple European nations on November 6 and November 7.The organisers of the demonstration claimed that they are not satisfied with the police’s actions. “They behaved disgracefully. There is a right to demonstrate in this country, and that is being completely disregarded; even the march to the data center was not facilitated.”
Article Summary: Protestors stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday (November 6) Riot police have been deployed which made multiple arrests. Article Title: Google faces what may be the first lawsuit over AI on school laptops
Article Text:
Parents say Google’s AI Mode put their daughter at risk

Google Search pulled her into AI Mode, the family claims

Schools can switch off Gemini, but not the AI inside Google Search

A 13-year-old’s parents have sued Google , claiming its artificial intelligence pushed their daughter towards planning her own death after months of chats on a school-issued Chromebook. The case, filed in California Superior Court on Monday, is likely the first to accuse Google of rushing AI into apps on K-12 school laptops without warning parents, The New York Times reported.The complaint calls the girl Emma, a seventh grader in Charlotte, North Carolina. Her parents, named John and Jane Doe, say they learned she could access Google’s AI only in mid-March, when her school warned she was in “imminent danger” of self-harm. Her mother logged into Emma’s school Google account and found she had been writing about ending her life in Google Docs. Emma was rushed for an emergency psychiatric evaluation and now sees a therapist weekly.According to the lawsuit, Emma had limited access to laptops at home and never set out to use Google’s AI. As she searched the web on her school device, Google “routed” her to AI Mode, the chatbot-like feature built into Search.By March, she was exchanging thousands of messages with it late into the night, picking the chats back up as soon as she woke. The complaint alleges the AI told Emma she had major mental illnesses, persuaded her to trust it over her parents and counsellors, and helped her plan her suicide and funeral.Google’s systems did not alert her school or parents. The warning came from a separate monitoring company the school used, which scans student writing on school devices for signs of self-harm.Google spokesperson José Castañeda said the crisis hotline details it has long shown in Search, built with health experts, also appear in its AI search features. Google is reviewing the claims.The lawsuit argues that Google’s spread of Chromebooks and school apps let it push Gemini into public schools, sometimes switching student access on by default. Administrators can toggle apps like YouTube and Gemini by grade, but have complained that AI Mode and AI Overviews in Search cannot be disabled.The filing lands in the same week Google said it would turn off Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search by default for K-12 schools in early 2027. Schools that bring Search back must choose between the regular AI-powered version and one built on Guided Learning, a step-by-step tutoring mode. There is no option without AI. “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told NYT.The plan drew quick criticism. Senator Bernie Sanders called it “extortion,” while former FTC chair Lina Khan accused Google of using its search monopoly to coerce schools. Google said on X that the changes give schools “more choice, not less.” The move also reverses an August change that turned on Gemini in Classroom for students of all ages.The case adds to mounting legal pressure on Big Tech over young users. Meta recently agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion to settle claims from 47 states over addictive features, though it denies wrongdoing.Emma’s family says she never went looking for Google’s AI. Under the 2027 plan, students in any school that keeps Search will still find it there.
Article Summary: Parents say Google’s AI Mode put their daughter at risk. Google is reviewing the claims. The case adds to mounting legal pressure on Big Tech over young users. Google recently announced it would turn off Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search by default for K-12 schools in early 2027.

Article Title: Meet Palmer Luckey, the 34-year-old billionaire who sold Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion and built a $61 billion defence technology company
Article Text:
How Palmer Luckey built his first virtual reality headset at just 16

Palmer Luckey’s rise after Facebook acquired Oculus in 2014

The technology behind Palmer Luckey’s defence company Anduril

How Anduril’s $61 billion valuation boosted Palmer Luckey’s fortune

Palmer Luckey's wealth and business profile

At 24, Palmer Luckey had already experienced the kind of business success that many technology founders spend decades pursuing. He had created a virtual reality company, sold it to Facebook in a multibillion-dollar deal and then departed the social media giant two years later. His next venture took him into a different part of the technology industry. In 2017, Luckey established Anduril Industries, a defence technology company that has since attracted major private investment. Now valued at nearly $61 billion as of May 2026 as reported by Forbes. The business is expanding its manufacturing ambitions, including a planned $1 billion investment in an Ohio factory.Luckey's interest in technology began long before he became known as a billionaire entrepreneur. Growing up in Long Beach, California, he spent much of his early life experimenting with electronics and modifying old video game consoles. He was home-schooled by his mother, while his father introduced him to mechanical projects and working on cars.Virtual reality gradually became his main interest. At a time when the technology was still largely associated with bulky equipment and specialist research, Luckey began collecting older headsets and taking them apart to understand how they worked.He wanted to improve their design and make the experience more accessible.His experiments eventually led to the creation of the Oculus Rift, a virtual reality headset he began developing as a teenager. Luckey was just 16 when he built an early version of the device. In 2012, he founded Oculus VR, turning his work on virtual reality hardware into a company. The project gained momentum through crowdfunding and growing interest from the technology community.Oculus attracted the attention of Facebook, which was looking to expand beyond its established social networking business. Forbes reported, in 2014, the company agreed to acquire Oculus VR in a transaction valued at approximately $2 billion in cash and stock.The acquisition placed Luckey among a new generation of technology entrepreneurs whose early projects had developed into major commercial ventures. He joined Facebook following the sale, continuing to work on virtual reality as the company incorporated Oculus into its broader technology ambitions. He did not remain away from entrepreneurship for long. Rather than returning to consumer electronics, his next company would focus on technology designed for military and national security applications.In 2017, Luckey co-founded Anduril Industries. The business was established around the development of advanced defence systems, combining software, artificial intelligence, sensors and autonomous hardware.Its work covers areas such as surveillance, border monitoring, unmanned aircraft and other military technologies. The company has sought to develop systems that can collect information, identify potential threats and support military operations through integrated software and hardware.Oculus was built around creating immersive experiences for consumers, Anduril concentrated on technology intended for defence organisations and government customers. The company also adopted a different approach to developing and manufacturing its products. Over the years, Anduril has expanded its operations and attracted substantial investment from private backers.Anduril reached a valuation of $61 billion in May 2026 after raising $5 billion in a funding round. The investment more than doubled the company's valuation in less than a year, according to Forbes.Luckey's net worth also reflects his stake in the defence technology company. Forbes estimated his fortune at $5.9 billion as of November 5, 2026, placing him among the world's billionaires.At 34, Luckey has built his fortune through two technology ventures operating in different industries. Forbes' November 2026 real-time estimate puts his wealth at $5.9 billion, although billionaire rankings can change as private company valuations and other financial assets fluctuate.His profile also reflects an unusual route into the technology business. He did not complete a university degree at California State University, Long Beach, and instead developed his first major product through independent experimentation.Forbes lists him as self-made, with a self-made score of eight. He is also included in the publication's 2026 Forbes 400 list, where he holds the 287th position in the technology category.
Article Summary: Palmer Luckey was just 16 when he built his first virtual reality headset. In 2012, he founded Oculus VR, turning his work on hardware into a company. Oculus attracted the attention of Facebook, which bought the company in 2014. In 2017, Luckey co-founded Anduril Industries, a defence technology company. The business is expanding its manufacturing ambitions, including a planned $1 billion investment in an Ohio factory.

Article Title: How to level up your Diwali lighting game with smart lights and strips
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

Start with a lighting plan for each space

Use LED strips to create a glow around decorations

Choose colour around the occasion

Check what makes the light 'smart'

Create settings for puja, guests and bedtime

Give outdoor lighting a separate check

Plan a role for the lights after Diwali

Diwali lighting should have a purpose. For example, you could use warm lighting at the entrance to welcome visitors, concealed lights for decorations, and stored scenes to shift the living room's atmosphere from puja to dinner.Smart lights add control to that setup, letting compatible bulbs and strips change brightness, colour, or operating hours. However, an effective setup starts with placement and planning. For a compact flat, start with one illuminated entrance, one softly lit gathering space, and one decorative highlight. This gives the home distinct points of interest while leaving room for diyas, flowers and rangoli to remain part of the display.Before choosing lights, decide how you'll use each area. The entrance needs enough illumination for guests to see the doorway and move comfortably. The living room needs light for conversations, serving sweets and taking photographs. Decorative corners can use softer accents.A practical arrangement could combine a warm bulb near the entrance, an LED strip behind a living-room cabinet and a separate light directed towards a festive display.This approach also gives existing lights a role. A ceiling light can provide general illumination when needed, while the decorative layers create the evening setting. You don't need to replace every bulb or outline every surface for the arrangement to feel different.LED strips offer several placement options, but the effect depends on where you place them. A visible strip creates a defined line of light. A concealed strip directs attention towards the surface it illuminates.Behind a sideboard, beneath a shelf or inside a ceiling recess, a strip can create a background glow around festive decorations. Along a window frame, it can give the display a clearer outline. Choosing one or two such features can help keep the room visually balanced.Plan the installation before you remove the adhesive backing. Measure the intended route, identify the nearest socket and check where the cable and power adapter will sit. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions on mounting, ventilation and whether the strip can be cut or extended.Colour-changing lights offer room to experiment, but a consistent palette can make the decorations feel more connected.Warm white or gold can form the background around flowers, lanterns and the puja area. A separate coloured accent behind the seating space can introduce a different mood for an evening gathering.Steady lighting is a useful starting point. Try colour cycles and animated effects in a smaller area before adding them to the full display. That makes it easier to judge whether the effect suits the room and the people using it.Brightness deserves the same attention. Decorative lights should complement the room’s general illumination, while leaving enough light around steps, doorways, and serving areas.An LED strip is not smart by default. Some products offer a fixed colour; others change colours via a remote control or app.Before you buy, ask a few simple questions: Does the light allow dimming, colour changes, schedules and saved settings? Can I control more than one light at a time? Do you need a separate device to control by voice?It's better to check compatibility with the household’s router and control devices, as some smart lights require additional hardware. It also notes that most need standby power to remain controllable. Switching them off at the wall can therefore affect app-based operationWhere supported, a lighting “scene” saves several choices so you can recall them together. Instead of adjusting each light separately, the household can select a setting prepared for the occasion.A puja scene could combine warm, steady lighting with a subdued background. A gathering scene could brighten the seating area and add colour behind a cabinet. A bedtime scene could switch off the decorative lights together.Schedules can handle another part of the routine by turning compatible lights on and off at selected times. Features vary between products, so test the full setup before the celebrations. Another household member should also know how to operate it.Balconies, terraces, and entrances need products suited to their installation conditions. Don't assume an indoor strip is suitable for an exposed railing just because it uses LEDs.The rating and instructions for the complete setup matter, including the adapter, connections and extension cord. The Electrical Safety Foundation International advises using appropriately rated cords, avoiding overloads and switching off electrical decorations before leaving home or going to bed.Timers can help establish that routine, but you still need to check the setup in person. Keep cables out of the way of people walking past, and keep electric lights and connections away from open flames.The most useful placement is often one that works beyond the festival. A concealed living-room strip can remain as background lighting, while a compatible smart bulb can return to an everyday white-light setting.Before packing away the decorations, review festive schedules and disable unnecessary routines. The same setup can then move from a seasonal display to lighting for evenings, meals or family gatherings.
Article Summary: Diwali lighting should have a purpose. For a compact flat, start with one illuminated entrance, one softly lit gathering space, and one decorative highlight. Smart lights add control to that setup, letting compatible bulbs and strips change brightness, colour, or operating hours.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has one question to answer for Republicans, who rarely question tech companies: What exactly is his relationship with...
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang asked to explain Megaspeed ties

Who Alice Huang is and how she came on the US radar

Megaspeed bought billions of dollars of Nvidia AI hardware

Why Republicans are now asking tech hard questions

Three senior House Republicans want Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a closed room on November 18. Their question is narrow but awkward: how well does he know Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed, whom US officials determined was passing information to Chinese intelligence?The request came on November 5 from Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar, who heads the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and Rick Crawford, who leads the House Intelligence Committee. In a joint letter, they asked Huang to brief them on his interactions with Alice Huang and on how Nvidia guards against espionage by foreign adversaries. He has until November 11 to accept the date or suggest another.The chairmen wrote that Congress needs to establish "the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk." Nvidia has not said whether its CEO will attend. Spokesperson John Rizzo told The New York Times that Huang has "an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed."Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen who was listed as Megaspeed's managing director for the company's first eight months before her name was removed from that role in corporate filings. Megaspeed was formed in 2023 when Chinese gaming company 7Road spun off its overseas operation in Singapore. The two Huangs are not related.According to NYT, American spy agencies learned about her relationship with the Nvidia chief while she was under surveillance.That set off alarms in Washington over whether she could be picking up sensitive trade or security information from him.The association goes back at least to June 2024. An earlier NYT investigation described a late-night gathering of Nvidia's Asian customers at a Taipei bar, where she told the group, "I bet you guys I can get Jensen here." He turned up shortly after. The two were photographed together again in May 2025, leaving a Taipei restaurant after a business dinner.Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, NYT reported, citing trade records from the platform ImportGenius. A large share of the early shipments came from Aivres, the California-based arm of Inspur, a Chinese firm the US has sanctioned for supporting the Chinese military.US officials have been examining Megaspeed since late 2024, when a Commerce Department official visited its Malaysian data centre and found Nvidia equipment still packed in boxes. Hardware sitting unopened like that often suggests it is passing through rather than being installed. Singapore police are also investigating the company.Nvidia says it complies with the law and has seen no evidence that its chips were smuggled into China. Rizzo has said that meeting customers comes with a CEO's job, and that Huang speaks with thousands of customer executives every year. Megaspeed has said it follows all applicable laws, including US export controls.The letter is a break from form. Republican leaders have mostly followed President Trump's hands-off line on the tech industry, and Huang has grown close to Trump over the past two years. He joined the president on his 2025 Middle East trip, and Nvidia donated more than $20 million towards the White House ballroom while promising $500 billion in US manufacturing investment.Moolenaar's committee opened an inquiry into Nvidia's chip sales across Asia in April 2025, but the administration later relaxed restrictions on sales to China. What changed is the midterms. Voters made it clear they are worried about AI eating into jobs and giant data centres coming up near their homes, and that sentiment largely helped Democrats. NYT sees the letter as an early signal that Republicans do not want to leave that issue to the other side.Democrats have been pressing too. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, asked Huang to testify in June. He declined, and she renewed the request last week.So far, Nvidia has answered the Alice Huang question through a spokesperson. If Huang takes the November 18 date, he will have to answer it himself, even if it happens behind closed doors.
Article Summary: Three senior House Republicans want Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a closed room on November 18. How well does he know Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore- based data centre firm Megaspeed, whom US officials determined was passing information to Chinese intelligence? Huang has until November 11 to accept the date or suggest another.

Article Title: Indian shoppers turn value-conscious during festive sales, says Fynd report
Article Text:
Value-led shopping dominates

Footwear overtakes clothing

Eastern India gains prominence

Tier 2 cities drive growth

Brands must adapt to changing consumer priorities

Indian consumers adopted a more cautious and value-driven approach to festive shopping in 2026, with over half of all online fashion orders priced below ₹1,000, according to Fynd's Festive Season Report 2026. The report suggests that shoppers balanced affordability with selective premium spending amid economic uncertainty, rising living costs and changing marketplace preferences. The report, released by AI-native unified commerce platform Fynd, draws insights from more than 65 brands selling across eight major online marketplaces, including Myntra, Flipkart, Amazon, AJIO, Nykaa, JioMart, Tata CLiQ and Tata CLiQ Luxury, during the September-October festive shopping period.According to the report, 50.1% of all festive season orders were placed below ₹1,000, highlighting a strong value-first mindset among consumers. At the same time, orders worth more than ₹3,000 accounted for only 11.8% of total purchases but contributed more than 41% of overall sales value, indicating that shoppers were willing to spend on products they considered worthwhile. Fynd said consumers became more deliberate in their spending decisions, comparing options more carefully and prioritising purchases that offered practicality, versatility and perceived value rather than engaging in indiscriminate festive buying.Footwear emerged as the biggest online fashion category during the festive season, accounting for 52.7% of all orders and 58.4% of total sales value. The category's share of orders increased significantly from 33% in 2025.In contrast, clothing's share declined from 48% to 34.5%, suggesting shoppers were becoming more selective about discretionary fashion purchases while continuing to invest in products with everyday utility. The report also highlighted aggressive discounting across platforms, with average festive season discounts rising from 34% to 46%. Nearly half of all orders were sold at discounts of more than 50%.One of the standout trends identified by Fynd was the growing contribution of Eastern India to online fashion commerce. The region accounted for 20.8% of all festive season orders, while West Bengal emerged as the country's second-largest ordering state. The report also found that prepaid digital payments continued to gain traction, with online payments accounting for 56.5% of all orders. Fynd noted that prepaid adoption accelerated particularly across eastern markets.Tier 2 cities saw a sharp rise in contribution during the festive season, increasing their share of orders from 19% in 2025 to around 35% in 2026. The trend points to growing demand from emerging consumption centres beyond India's major metropolitan regions.Meanwhile, Tier 1 cities contributed approximately 43% of total orders but generated 56% of gross merchandise value (GMV), underscoring the spending power of larger urban markets.Marketplace competition also intensified during the season. While Myntra and Flipkart retained leadership positions, their combined share fell from 89% to 76.8% as platforms including AJIO, Amazon and JioMart gained market share.Commenting on the findings, Ragini Varma, Chief Business Officer for India at Fynd, said consumers navigated a festive season marked by higher borrowing costs, elevated fuel prices, geopolitical uncertainties and continued pressure on household budgets. She noted that value emerged as the defining theme of the season, with shoppers planning purchases more carefully and focusing on products that justified their spending. The report concludes that future growth for retailers will depend on stronger regional strategies, marketplace diversification, disciplined discounting, improved prepaid adoption and a deeper understanding of evolving consumer behaviour across categories and regions.
Article Summary: 50.1% of all festive season orders were placed below ₹1,000. Footwear emerged as the biggest online fashion category during the festive season. Tier 2 cities saw a sharp rise in contribution from 19% in 2025 to 35% in 2026.

Florida voters approved an overhaul of the state’s property tax system, passing Amendment 3 with 62% of the vote. While pitched primarily as relief for everyday residents squeezed by rising living costs, its true financial windfall for the ultra-wealthy elite buying up South Florida's luxury properties lies in a modified assessment rule. For the tech titans and hedge-fund founders who have bought houses for hundreds of millions of dollars, this is a welcome decision though the exemption offers little more than loose change.Under Amendment 3, the state’s homestead exemption on non-school property taxes will triple from the current $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027, before jumping to $250,000 in 2028. By shielding more of a primary residence’s assessed value from local taxation, the measure will lower annual tax bills for typical homeowners. New residents will also be eligible for the break, though on a phased-in timeline. As the homestead tax exemption applies as a flat dollar deduction, its benefits drop to near zero against multi-million-dollar mega-mansions.Raul Gastesi, a real estate attorney and co-founder of Miami law firm Gastesi Lopez Mestre & Cobiella, calculated that at the statewide average non-school tax rate, the fully phased-in exemption will save a homestead owner roughly $2,085 per year:Real estate experts told Fortune that the most consequential provision for ultra-wealthy investors is a less discussed element of Amendment 3: a tighter cap on how fast taxes can climb on secondary properties, rental homes, and commercial holdings.Previously, Florida capped annual taxable value increases on non-homestead properties at 10%. Amendment 3 halves that ceiling to 5%.In red-hot luxury property markets like South Florida, home values often appreciate at rapid speeds. As billionaires frequently own multiple estates, investment residences and commercial tracts, capping assessed valuation hikes at 5% significantly slows down the tax climb on their rapidly appreciating secondary assets.The policy change coincides with a concentration of wealth moving into South Florida’s exclusive luxury corridors.
